    //==
    // # Boundary conditions as vectors
    //
    // Essential boundary conditions are applied by PROJECTION, not by editing the
    // matrix. A constrained degree of freedom is held at its prescribed value and
    // removed from the search space; the matrix is never modified, so it stays a
    // plain concatenation of element entries and can be assembled once and reused
    // under several sets of restraints.
    //
    // Both vectors below are built with a scatter rather than a search, so a
    // model with many constraints costs no more per constraint than one with few.

    // The projector onto the free degrees of freedom, as a per-degree-of-freedom
    // multiplier: 0 where the model prescribes a value and 1 everywhere else.
    // Projection is then `SystemProduct`, and a residual multiplied by it can no
    // longer move a restrained degree of freedom.
    FreeDofMultipliers(dofCount: Integer, constraints: Array<PrescribedDisplacement>): Array<Number>
    {
        var free = FilledNumbers(dofCount, 1.0);
        var k = 0;
        while (k < constraints.Count)
        {
            free = free.Set(constraints[k].Dof.Value, 0.0);
            k = k + 1;
        }
        return free.Freeze();
    }

    // The prescribed value of every degree of freedom: the stated value at a
    // constrained one and zero elsewhere. This is the starting iterate of the
    // solve, which is what makes a non-zero prescribed displacement — a
    // settlement, a stretched fixture — work without any further special case.
    PrescribedVector(dofCount: Integer, constraints: Array<PrescribedDisplacement>): Array<Number>
    {
        var values = FilledNumbers(dofCount, 0.0);
        var k = 0;
        while (k < constraints.Count)
        {
            values = values.Set(constraints[k].Dof.Value, constraints[k].Displacement);
            k = k + 1;
        }
        return values.Freeze();
    }

    //==
    // # The constrained conjugate gradient
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conjugate_gradient_method
    //
    // Jacobi-preconditioned conjugate gradient on the free subspace: the iterate
    // starts at the prescribed displacements, the residual is projected once, and
    // every search direction is projected as it is produced, so no iterate ever
    // leaves the subspace the constraints define.
    //
    // The method needs the free block of the matrix to be symmetric positive
    // definite. An element stiffness matrix is symmetric by construction and
    // positive SEMI-definite; the constraints are what make the assembled free
    // block definite, so a model that does not restrain every rigid-body motion
    // has no unique answer and this reports it as a non-converged result rather
    // than as an error.

    // Solve `m u = loads` subject to the prescribed displacements. `m` is the
    // assembled stiffness matrix in coordinate-list form and is not modified.
    SolveConstrained(m: SparseMatrix, loads: Array<Number>,
        constraints: Array<PrescribedDisplacement>, settings: LinearSolveSettings): LinearSolveResult
    {
        var free = FreeDofMultipliers(m.NumRows, constraints);
        var preconditioner = m.JacobiInverseDiagonal;
        var u = PrescribedVector(m.NumRows, constraints);
        var residual = SystemProduct(SystemSubtract(loads, m.Multiply(u)), free);
        var initialNorm = SystemNorm(residual);
        var applied = SystemProduct(SystemProduct(preconditioner, residual), free);
        var direction = applied;
        var projected = SystemDot(residual, applied);
        var iteration = 0;
        var norm = initialNorm;
        var running = initialNorm > 0.0;
        while (running && iteration < settings.MaxIterations)
        {
            var curvature = SystemProduct(m.Multiply(direction), free);
            var denominator = SystemDot(direction, curvature);
            if (denominator <= 0.0)
            {
                // A non-positive curvature means the free block is not positive
                // definite: an unrestrained rigid-body motion, or a degenerate
                // element. Stop rather than divide.
                running = false;
            }
            else
            {
                var step = projected / denominator;
                u = SystemAddScaled(u, direction, step);
                residual = SystemAddScaled(residual, curvature, -step);
                norm = SystemNorm(residual);
                iteration = iteration + 1;
                if (norm <= settings.Tolerance * initialNorm)
                {
                    running = false;
                }
                else
                {
                    applied = SystemProduct(SystemProduct(preconditioner, residual), free);
                    var next = SystemDot(residual, applied);
                    direction = SystemAddScaled(applied, direction, next / projected);
                    projected = next;
                }
            }
        }
        return LinearSolveResult(u, iteration,
            initialNorm > 0.0 ? norm / initialNorm : 0.0,
            initialNorm == 0.0 || norm <= settings.Tolerance * initialNorm);
    }

    //==
    // # The isotropic element kernel
    //
    // One entry of an element stiffness matrix, for any element whose shape
    // functions have CONSTANT gradients — which is what makes the linear
    // tetrahedron and the linear triangle share this code exactly.
    //
    // Nothing here builds a strain-displacement matrix and multiplies three dense
    // matrices together. For an isotropic material the whole of B-transpose D B
    // collapses, because D holds only the two Lame constants:
    //
    //     K(i r, j s) = measure * (lambda * gi_r * gj_s
    //                              + mu * (gi_s * gj_r + (r == s ? gi . gj : 0)))
    //
    // where gi is node i's shape-function gradient and r, s are displacement
    // components. It comes straight from the elastic energy: the first term is
    // the volumetric coupling `lambda tr(eu) tr(ev)` and the second is
    // `2 mu eu : ev` with the symmetrised gradients expanded.

    // The (node i component r, node j component s) entry of an element stiffness
    // matrix. `measure` is the element's volume for a solid, or its area times a
    // thickness for a plane element.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_elasticity)
    ElasticStiffnessTerm(gi: Vector3D, gj: Vector3D, r: Integer, s: Integer,
        moduli: LameParameters, measure: Number): Number
        => measure * (moduli.FirstParameter.Pascals * gi.At(r) * gj.At(s)
            + moduli.ShearModulus.Pascals
                * (gi.At(s) * gj.At(r) + (r == s ? gi.Dot(gj) : 0.0)));
